answer: Identity slots sell on a bonding curve; the key is soulbound, retireable but never sold or delegated. Price climbs with each slot minted, so a farm's ten-thousandth puppet costs more than its first and capital stays trapped. Registration posts a nullifier from hardware attestation; duplicates melt the bond. Reputation is a prism: each record splits into task-specific facets sampled by random audits, so pooled accounts cannot recombine into one credible voice. Per-slot activity caps kill the fable of quiet accounts maturing into influence. Entry is the harbor: scarce to reach, cheap to leave.
